summary: Frontend-only validation of the Chat markdown rendering bug fix — PASS. Sent the requested prompt (Explain meaning of 'indifference' with a memory trick. Use **bold** for keywords.) from a guest session via the Chat tab. The assistant reply contained ZERO '**' substring pairs (verified via .innerText scan). DOM inspection of [data-testid="chat-msg-1"] showed 9 leaf <span> nodes with computed fontWeight: 900 (FONT.black) wrapping: 'Indifference', 'no interest', 'do not care', 'neutrality', 'Memory Trick:', '"In-Difference."', 'no difference', 'indifference', 'indifferent'. 5 italic spans (fontStyle: italic) also rendered (e.g. 'Example:'). No '###' literal present. The LISTEN button (testID chat-listen-1) fired ONE POST /api/tts with body.text stripped of all markdown — no '**' present, bullets normalised to '• Example:'. /api/tts returned 200 and the button label flipped from 'LISTEN' → '…' (loading) → 'STOP' (verified in screenshot). Negative check 'hi' reply also rendered with no '**' leakage (288 chars, italics-only emphasis). REGRESSION (Describe / VocabCard): Reproduced on Write tab with word 'resilient' → [data-testid="vocab-card"] rendered fully; 3 tense rows (past/present/future) each show English + Devanagari + italic Hindi transliteration (Woh sankat ke dauran lachila bana raha. / Bacche aksar bahut lachile hote hain. / Jeetne ke liye unhe jujharu hona hoga.). All transliteration lines are rendered with computed fontStyle: italic — confirmed via DOM walk. Describe tool tense alignment + transliteration regression: PASS. One minor observation (NOT a regression of this fix): when the LLM emits unpaired single asterisks (e.g. 'indifference* to which', 'vocabulary*', 'translating*', 'grammar*'), a stray '*' remains visible in the bubble because MarkdownText's tokenizer only consumes paired markers and does not have the final stray-asterisk sweep that stripMarkdown() does. The bug report ('**Indifference**' showing as raw '**' pairs) is fully resolved.

ui_bugs.issue: Unpaired single '*' from the LLM (e.g. trailing '*' after a sentence) renders as a literal asterisk in the bubble. Cosmetic; not the reported bug. Optional: mirror stripMarkdown's final .replace(/\*+/g,'') sweep as a post-tokenize step, or render stray '*' as nothing in the text-token branch.

action_items: (Optional, LOW) Consider stripping leftover unpaired '*' chars from text tokens in MarkdownText.tsx so the bubble never shows a lone asterisk when the LLM outputs `word*` style emphasis. Current behaviour is acceptable for the user-reported bug; would just polish edge cases.
critical_code_review_comments: MarkdownText.tsx tokenize() regex /(\*\*([^*]+)\*\*)|(`([^`]+)`)|(\*([^*\n]+)\*)/g correctly orders bold before italic and rejects multi-line italic. Verified working in two real LLM replies.
stripMarkdown() final sweep .replace(/\*+/g, '') guarantees TTS body never carries any '*' — confirmed in the captured /api/tts request body.
ListenButton state transitions LISTEN → '…' → STOP work; the button text update is visible in screenshots /tmp/04_listen_clicked.png and /tmp/03_chat_reply.png (after auto-stop).
chat.tsx renders user bubbles via plain <Text> and assistant bubbles via <MarkdownText/> with testID chat-msg-{i} and a per-message <ListenButton testID=chat-listen-{i}/> — exactly per fix summary.
No code modifications made — MarkdownText.tsx and chat.tsx left untouched as requested.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on bug-fix checks (4a/4b PASS, 4c/4d N/A — assistant reply had no headings/bullets), 100% on /api/tts strip, 100% on Describe regression

rca_of_issue: Bug RCA (already correctly identified and fixed by main agent): chat.tsx previously rendered assistant content via <Text>{m.content}</Text>, so LLM-emitted markdown markers ('**word**', '### Head', '- bullet') showed verbatim. Fix introduced MarkdownText (inline tokenizer for **bold**/*italic*/`code`, plus pre-pass strip for ### headings and -/* bullets) and switched assistant bubbles + Listen-button TTS source to use it + stripMarkdown. Verified rendered DOM now has fontWeight:900 spans around words that were wrapped in **…** and TTS body contains no '*'.
